scored.title: End-to-end multimodal pathology foundation model with clinical dialogue.
scored.why: PRISM2 is a multimodal pathology foundation model trained on 2.3 million whole-slide images and 14 million question-answer pairs derived from pathology reports, and it matches or exceeds the balanced accuracy of clinical-grade cancer detection products in prostate, breast, and breast lymph node tissue (P<0.05). This is a large-scale, benchmarked advance in computational pathology showing that language-supervised pretraining can produce generalizable diagnostic representations, though real-world deployment validation is still needed.

scored.title: Multicenter Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence System for Automatic Recognition of Fetal Ultrasound Findings Suggestive of Congenital Malformations.
scored.why: This multicenter retrospective evaluation tested an artificial intelligence (AI) system for detecting eight abnormal fetal ultrasound findings suggestive of congenital malformations across 6,452 images from 1,115 examinations at 75 international sites, achieving mean sensitivity of 93.2% and specificity of 90.8% with consistent performance across manufacturers, regions, and demographics. The large, geographically diverse multicenter dataset and rigorous ground-truth methodology make this one of the more generalizable evaluations of AI in fetal anomaly screening, though it remains a retrospective still-image analysis rather than a prospective real-time clinical trial.

scored.title: Tipping the balance: impact of class imbalance correction on the performance of clinical risk prediction models.
scored.why: Across ten clinical datasets covering over 600,000 patients and multiple machine-learning model families, class-imbalance correction methods like synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) did not improve area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) or precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) but consistently worsened calibration, as measured by Brier score increases of 0.029 to 0.080. This is a methodologically rigorous, multi-dataset demonstration that a widely used technique for handling rare outcomes can distort predicted probabilities without improving discrimination, which matters directly for anyone building or evaluating clinical risk models.

scored.title: Risk Stratification for Postpartum Hemorrhage in Vaginal Delivery: A Nationwide Cohort Study of Predelivery and Intrapartum Risk Assessment.
scored.why: This nationwide retrospective cohort study of 1,224,990 vaginal deliveries in Japan developed machine learning models for postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) risk stratification, using 2014-2022 data for training and reserving 2023 for temporal external validation, where adding intrapartum data improved sensitivity from 0.537 to 0.596 and discrimination (area under the curve, AUC) from 0.676 to 0.703 at a fixed alert-rate threshold. The huge sample size, genuine temporal external validation, and clinically interpretable metrics (cases detected per 1000 deliveries) make this one of the more rigorous obstetric AI risk-prediction studies this cycle, though the absolute discrimination gains remain modest.

scored.title: Leveraging administrative health records and machine learning for population-level prediction of preterm birth.
scored.why: This retrospective population-based cohort study of 328,834 singleton pregnancies in Alberta, Canada developed several machine learning models, including gradient-boosted trees and transformer-based architectures, to predict preterm birth at 26 weeks using only administrative health records, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.7704 on a temporally separated holdout set of 67,186 pregnancies from later years. The large scale, chronologically split validation, and use of routinely available data rather than specialized tests make this a credible step toward scalable population-level screening, though the AUC remains moderate and true external validation in another health system is still needed.

scored.title: Explainable TabNet for gestational diabetes prediction with physician-in-the-loop and multi-site clinical validation.
scored.why: This study developed an explainable TabNet deep learning model for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) prediction using first-antenatal-visit clinical features from 3,525 records, achieving 97.13% accuracy in cross-validation, and then conducted a genuine two-stage physician-in-the-loop (PITL) evaluation plus prospective external validation across three independent Kerala hospitals, where F1-scores dropped to 83.7% to 87.0%, reflecting realistic real-world performance decay. The combination of explainability tools (SHAP, LIME), formal clinician trust assessment, and true multi-site external validation is unusually rigorous for this literature and directly relevant to how such tools might be evaluated before deployment, though the drop from internal to external performance underscores the gap between benchmark and real-world results.

scored.title: First-Trimester Machine Learning to Predict Preeclampsia in Normotensive Pregnancies by American Heart Association Guidelines.
scored.why: This prospective cohort study across two academic centers applied unsupervised machine learning (k-means clustering) to first-trimester blood pressure data in normotensive pregnancies by American Heart Association (AHA) guidelines, identifying a high-risk subgroup with an eight-fold increased adjusted hazard ratio (aHR 8.01) for preeclampsia despite normal blood pressure readings. This is a clinically meaningful finding that could reshape early risk stratification in obstetrics, though it needs external validation before changing practice given its origin from a secondary analysis of two-center data.

scored.title: Generative artificial intelligence for inpatient documentation summarization: mixed-methods quality assessment and early real-world experience.
scored.why: In a pragmatic mixed-methods evaluation across three tertiary-care academic hospitals, a large language model (LLM)-based inpatient documentation summarization tool received favorable ratings (mean 4.68 of 5) across all nine domains of the Provider Documentation Summarization Quality Instrument (PDSQI-9), though the survey response rate was low (10.2%, 52 of 512 users). This is a real-world, multi-site deployment assessment with both quantitative and qualitative feedback, offering useful signal on clinician acceptance despite limited response and lack of a comparator arm or patient outcome data.

scored.title: Sociodemographic bias in large language model clinical trial screening.
scored.why: Across 58 phase II-III randomized controlled trial (RCT) protocols and 5.3 million evaluations, nine large language models (LLMs) showed largely stable eligibility judgments across 33 sociodemographic identity variants, but homelessness produced the largest negative shift in eligibility and related domains like adherence and trust. This is a large-scale, systematic fairness audit relevant to anyone considering LLM-assisted trial screening, showing that bias emerges specifically in inferential judgments about resources and behavior rather than explicit criteria application.

scored.title: Multi-modal Stacking Machine Learning Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Cervical Cancer.
scored.why: This retrospective study with external validation built a stacking ensemble machine learning model combining Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) habitat radiomics with clinical variables to predict lymph node metastasis in 623 early-stage cervical cancer patients, achieving area under the curve (AUC) of 0.875 in the external cohort versus 0.845-0.865 for the best single base model, confirmed by DeLong test and decision curve analysis. The multi-cohort design with genuine external validation is a methodological strength, though the gain over the best base learner is modest and the model still needs prospective testing before it could guide surgical decisions.

scored.source: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
scored.title: Agreement between expert gynecologists and ChatGPT in the management of suspected retained products of conception.
scored.why: In this prospective comparative study of 50 real clinical cases of suspected retained products of conception (RPOC), ChatGPT version 5.2 showed substantially lower agreement with expert gynecologist consensus (accuracy 34.0% to 54.0%, Cohen's kappa 0.27 to 0.33) than physicians agreed with each other (82.7% accuracy, kappa 0.58). This is a well-designed head-to-head evaluation against a real clinical reference standard showing current large language models (LLMs) are not yet reliable as independent decision-makers in this obstetric management scenario, which is directly useful for calibrating expectations about LLM deployment in clinical workflows.

scored.title: Artificial intelligence-driven oocyte scores are associated with early morphokinetics and embryo outcomes after intracytoplasmic sperm injection.
scored.why: This retrospective study of 2,785 oocyte images from 1,340 intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) cycles used the deep-learning-based scoring system MAGENTA and found that higher oocyte scores were associated with better fertilization rates, favorable morphokinetic timing, blastocyst development, and cumulative live birth rate (all P<0.001). The sizeable sample and linkage to a hard clinical endpoint, live birth, strengthen confidence in the tool's biological validity as an oocyte quality marker, though the retrospective single-technology design still requires prospective clinical trial confirmation before influencing embryo selection practice.

scored.title: Prevalence and determinants of sacroiliac joint bone marrow oedema in the general population in Germany: a population-based cross-sectional study.
scored.why: This population-based cross-sectional study of 11,163 adults from the German National Cohort used a validated deep-learning algorithm to automatically segment and quantify sacroiliac bone marrow oedema on whole-body MRI, finding it present in roughly 30% of the general population, about 50 times higher than the reported prevalence of axial spondyloarthritis diagnosis, with women showing higher prevalence (33.9% vs 27.8% in men) partly linked to pregnancy history. This large-scale application of automated deep learning to a population imaging cohort provides an important calibration point against overdiagnosis when interpreting MRI findings in suspected inflammatory arthritis, and its methodological rigor (expert-reader comparison, multivariable adjustment) generalizes well beyond the specific reproductive finding.

scored.title: Performance evaluation of large language models in real-world perinatal medication consultations: a cross-sectional study.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study evaluated seven large language models (LLMs), including GPT-5.1, Grok 3, and DeepSeek, on 64 real-world Chinese perinatal medication consultation questions drawn from over 15,000 clinical records, with senior clinical pharmacologists rating responses on relevance, accuracy, usefulness, and empathy; GPT-5.1 scored highest (median 9.3 of 10) with excellent inter-rater consistency (intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) 0.91). This provides a useful real-world comparative benchmark for LLM performance in a high-stakes, benefit-risk-sensitive clinical pharmacy task, though it stops short of assessing actual patient outcomes or integration into live clinical workflows.

scored.title: Deep learning for Evaluation and Prediction of TecHnical Skills in robotic-assisted vaginal cuff closure study.
scored.why: This multicenter prospective observational cohort study used deep learning on video from robotic-assisted vaginal cuff closures to predict surgical errors and skill level, showing good interrater reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.807) and strong agreement between model and manual skill ratings (r=0.85). The proof-of-concept design across two centers with 40 videos is a meaningful step toward automated surgical skill assessment, though sample size is modest and it targets surgical training rather than patient outcomes directly.

scored.title: Loss function influence on hyperparameter optimization for observational healthcare prediction models.
scored.why: Using fifteen loss function metrics across three clinical prediction tasks and four machine-learning algorithms, this study found that hyperparameters optimized for area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) often did not produce the best-performing models by that same metric, and that choice of loss function metric substantially altered individual patient-level predicted risk despite similar population-level discrimination and calibration. This methodological finding on predictive multiplicity is relevant to anyone deploying risk models, since it shows that population-level validation metrics can mask clinically meaningful instability in individual predictions.

scored.title: What do clinicians edit in ambient AI-drafted clinical documentation? A qualitative content analysis.
scored.why: This qualitative content analysis of 200 clinical encounters found that clinicians most frequently edited ambient artificial intelligence (AI)-generated documentation for factual errors involving orders, symptoms, medications, and diagnoses, rather than terminology or style. The study offers real-world, actionable insight into where ambient AI scribes currently fail clinically, though it is descriptive and does not quantify downstream safety or efficiency impact.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence Based Ultrasound Screening for Antenatal Detection of Placenta Accreta Spectrum.
scored.why: In a retrospective single-center study of 113 at-risk patients and nearly 39,000 ultrasound image frames, a convolutional neural network combined with clinical risk factors predicted placenta accreta spectrum with 100% sensitivity, 75% specificity, and area under the curve (AUC) of 0.972, though confidence intervals were wide given the small test set. This is a promising first demonstration of image-based AI screening for a serious, often under-diagnosed obstetric condition, but it requires prospective, multi-center validation before clinical adoption given the retrospective single-center design and small sample.

scored.title: Improving laboratory workforce efficiency using AI-assisted digital cytology within an HPV-based cervical screening programme: A model-based evaluation for the NHS Cervical Screening Programmes.
scored.why: This decision-tree modeling study estimated that AI-assisted digital cytology would cut cervical screening slide review time from 12.9 to 4.0 minutes per slide, reducing annual staff hours by roughly 69% across the English National Health Service (NHS) cervical screening program, based on published evidence rather than a new prospective trial. It is a policy-relevant workforce projection rather than a clinical outcome study, so it speaks to operational feasibility of AI-assisted cytology rather than diagnostic performance or patient outcomes.

scored.title: An explainable machine learning approach for cervical cancer screening: decoding morphological diagnostic drivers.
scored.why: This retrospective study audited 5,000 archived liquid-based cytology slides using an interpretable machine learning pipeline (LBC-NET) against double-blind cytopathologist review, finding higher sensitivity for high-grade lesions (92.5% versus 84.2%, area under the curve, AUC, 0.94) with no performance loss across menopausal or infection subgroups, and Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based feature attribution. The retrospective single-network design without a separate external validation cohort limits generalizability, but the combination of subgroup robustness testing and interpretability analysis is more thorough than typical single-center AUC papers.

scored.title: Performance of Large Language Model-Based Chatbots in Primary Health Care Teleconsultations: A Comparison Between Human and Artificial Intelligence-Generated Responses.
scored.why: This blinded comparative cross-sectional study evaluated 180 human versus large language model (LLM)-generated responses to real primary care teleconsultation queries across cardiology, endocrinology, and obstetrics/gynecology (OB-GYN), finding AI responses scored as more comprehensible with no significant difference in medical adequacy or risk, though evaluators could reliably distinguish AI from human authorship. The blinded design and inclusion of an OB-GYN subgroup make this a reasonably rigorous real-world comparison, though it is a single-site Brazilian telehealth program and does not measure downstream patient outcomes.

scored.title: Risk-prediction models for postpartum depression: Assessment of risk of bias using PROBAST+AI.
scored.why: This systematic review evaluated 13 studies encompassing 64 postpartum depression (PPD) risk prediction models using PROBAST+AI (Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool), finding high risk of bias in 10 of 13 development studies and 12 of 13 validation studies, primarily due to poor participant representativeness and predictor handling. This meta-level appraisal is useful for calibrating skepticism toward the broader PPD prediction literature, though it offers no new model or data, only a critical synthesis of existing methodological weaknesses.

scored.title: Enhancing agreement in cardiotocography interpretation between midwives and obstetricians through a rule-based AI program: A comparative cross-sectional study.
scored.why: This comparative cross-sectional study tested a rule-based artificial intelligence (AI) program built on National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) guidelines to improve agreement between midwives and obstetricians in interpreting cardiotocography (CTG) traces, showing kappa improvement from moderate (0.548) to almost perfect (0.906) and reduced interpretation time. The design is a small, single-context exploratory study without a neonatal outcome or external gold standard, so it demonstrates interrater agreement improvement rather than proven clinical benefit.

scored.title: Perceptions of simulated artificial intelligence in medical consultations: associations with stress, memory, and perceived credibility.
scored.why: In a Wizard-of-Oz simulated study with 163 healthy participants, consultations perceived as delivered by an AI physician produced lower stress (including salivary cortisol) and lower memory retrieval than human-delivered consultations, with higher perceived credibility linked to greater stress. The design used no real AI system and only healthy volunteers in simulated bad-news scenarios, so findings on trust and stress are preliminary and limited in generalizability to actual clinical AI deployment.

scored.title: Optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in clinical medicine: methods and performance evaluation.
scored.why: Using four open-source large language models (LLMs) and a five-textbook sleep medicine knowledge base, this study found retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improved board-style multiple choice question (MCQ) accuracy by up to 10.6 percentage points, with hybrid sparse-dense retrieval and structured corpora outperforming raw text and dense-only retrieval. The work is a useful engineering benchmark for RAG pipeline design in a narrow specialty, but it is confined to text-based question answering without any prospective clinical evaluation or patient-facing deployment.

scored.title: Ultrasound-based machine learning models for assisting the prediction of neonatal size and mode of delivery.
scored.why: In a retrospective single-center cohort of 3,447 pregnant women, machine learning models using only three prenatal ultrasound measurements predicted newborn weight comparably to the standard Hadlock IV formula and predicted head circumference better than the last prenatal ultrasound estimate, with delivery mode classification linked to high predicted values. The study is retrospective, single-center, and lacks external validation, limiting confidence that these accuracy gains would generalize to other populations or change delivery management.

scored.title: Predicting Response to Radiotherapy in Locally Advanced Cervical Squamous Cell Carcinoma Based on Multisequence MRI and Clinical Variables.
scored.why: In a retrospective study of 248 patients with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma, a deep learning radiomics model combining multisequence magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with clinical variables predicted tumor shrinkage rate after external beam radiotherapy (EBRT), with fusion models reaching area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.824 to 0.863, outperforming single-sequence models. The study used only internal train-validation splitting from a single center without external validation, so the model's generalizability to other institutions or scanners remains unproven.

scored.title: Elevated Circulating AIF1L as a Cell-Free RNA Biomarker of Preeclampsia Impairs Trophoblast Function via Mitochondrial Dysregulation.
scored.why: This study integrated placental and plasma transcriptomic data with machine learning to derive a 10-gene cell-free RNA (cfRNA) nomogram for preeclampsia (area under the curve, AUC, 0.989) and used single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) plus trophoblast cell line experiments to implicate AIF1L in mitochondrial dysregulation. The extremely high AUC from a single-cohort machine learning model without described external validation is a red flag for overfitting, and the mechanistic claims rest on in vitro trophoblast assays rather than in vivo or clinical confirmation.

scored.title: AI-derived oocyte morphology and follicular fluid biomarkers in donors.
scored.why: This small correlational study of 49 oocyte donors linked artificial intelligence (AI)-derived oocyte morphology scores to follicular fluid biomarkers such as glucose, cholesterol, anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH), and HSPG2/Perlecan, aiming to explain what biological features the AI score captures. The sample size is modest, associations are exploratory and correlational rather than predictive of clinical outcomes like live birth, so this is hypothesis-generating work on interpretability of an existing AI tool rather than a validated new capability.

scored.title: Data-driven endocrine-metabolic phenotypes in young women with polycystic ovary syndrome and associations with cardiometabolic risk markers.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study of 1,032 young women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) used principal component analysis (PCA) and Gaussian mixture model clustering, an unsupervised statistical approach rather than a predictive AI model, to identify a thyroid/autoimmune-enriched subgroup associated with modestly worse lipid profiles. The clustering is exploratory and unvalidated externally, and while the sample size is respectable for a single tertiary center, the authors themselves caution that findings need longitudinal confirmation before informing clinical subtyping.

scored.title: Prenatal environmental exposures associated with ADHD diagnosis in children: a multicentre exposome analysis.
scored.why: This multicohort study of 156,563 children used a Random Forest machine learning model to rank prenatal environmental exposures by predictive importance for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), then confirmed via random-effects meta-analysis that maternal smoking (odds ratio 1.67) and low maternal education (odds ratio 1.62) were associated with increased ADHD odds. The machine learning step functioned mainly as a variable-selection tool rather than a predictive or diagnostic model, and the substantive findings are epidemiological associations already familiar from prior literature, with residual confounding from gene-environment correlation acknowledged by the authors.

scored.title: In Vivo Assessment of Placental Structure and Perfusion in Late-Gestation Pregnancies and Their Association With Fetal Growth.
scored.why: This prospective study used advanced MRI with deep-learning-assisted image processing to characterize placental perfusion and structure in 46 appropriate-for-gestational-age and 11 fetal growth restriction (FGR) pregnancies, finding that umbilical-cord centricity index and arterial-transit-time radiomics features best distinguished FGR from normal pregnancies. The deep learning component here is a supporting tool for image quantification rather than the primary contribution, and the very small sample size, especially in the FGR group, limits generalizability despite the mechanistic interest of the perfusion findings.

scored.source: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
scored.title: Machine learning models for non-invasive endometriosis triage using a laparoscopically and histologically verified cohort.
scored.why: This retrospective study of 2,546 laparoscopically and histologically verified cases from two Brazilian tertiary centers developed machine learning models, best an XGBoost classifier, for non-invasive endometriosis triage using structured clinical variables, achieving an F1-score of 0.916 and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.895 with internal 10-fold cross-validation. The enriched disease prevalence (77.9%) in a tertiary referral population and lack of external validation limit generalizability to typical clinical settings where prevalence and case mix differ substantially.

scored.title: A novel predictive model for evaluating thrombus regression in postpartum venous thromboembolism patients.
scored.why: A random forest model predicting thrombus regression in postpartum venous thromboembolism (VTE) was developed on a retrospective cohort (n=200) and tested on small prospective (n=50) and external (n=29) cohorts, reaching an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.831 but with low sensitivity (0.45). The multi-cohort design is a plus, but the tiny validation samples and poor sensitivity limit clinical usefulness for this postpartum-specific application.

scored.title: Clinician-perceived clinical accuracy and guideline alignment of ChatGPT responses to patient questions on HPV and CIN: a two-year comparative evaluation.
scored.why: This longitudinal study had five gynecologists rate ChatGPT's responses to ten frequently asked patient questions about human papillomavirus (HPV) and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) at two timepoints, finding favorable perceived accuracy (88-92%) but poor inter-rater reliability, with Fleiss' kappa below zero indicating agreement worse than chance. The small question set, subjective rating design, and lack of objective guideline benchmarking make this weak evidence for clinical deployment of chatbot-generated patient education.

scored.title: The use of structured prompt to improve the readability, accuracy, and quality of ChatGPT responses on labor epidural analgesia: a brief report.
scored.why: This brief report tested whether a structured prompting technique, the Context Role Action Format Tone (CRAFT) framework, improved readability and accuracy of ChatGPT-5.2 responses to 29 questions on labor epidural analgesia, finding improved readability (down to 6th-9th grade level) and a small but statistically significant accuracy gain (99.8% versus 99.0%, P=0.029). The sample of 29 questions and single-model, single-prompt-style comparison limits generalizability, and the accuracy difference, while statistically significant, is clinically marginal.

scored.title: The promise of deep urine proteomics for diagnosis of cancer, neurologic, and metabolic diseases.
scored.why: This case-control diagnostic accuracy study used deep urine proteomics and machine learning on only 264 samples (22 per disease group) across nine conditions including three gynecologic cancers, reporting area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values up to 0.98 for ovarian cancer. The design is exploratory with tiny per-group sample sizes and no external validation, so the authors themselves flag these as upper-bound estimates rather than clinically actionable results.

scored.title: Evidence integration: The transformative role of artificial intelligence in maternal health.
scored.why: This umbrella review synthesizes 34 existing reviews on artificial intelligence (AI) applications in maternal health, concluding that a persistent translation gap exists around external validation, interpretability, and prospective impact evaluation. As a review of reviews rather than new evidence, it offers a useful orientation to the field's gaps but no new data or finding for this reader to act on.

scored.title: Fusion Gene Detection Enhances Clinical Outcome Prediction of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Through Machine Learning Analyses.
scored.why: This retrospective study of 200 hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) samples used machine learning to show that adding a 20-gene fusion panel to clinical parameters (Milan criteria, alpha-fetoprotein, pathology grade) improved 3-year survival prediction accuracy to 72.4% from a baseline of 49-70.2% for individual factors. This is a single-cohort retrospective biomarker discovery study without external validation, and while it is a substantial general oncology clinical AI application, it has no reproductive relevance and modest methodological rigor.

scored.title: Machine Learning Analysis of Maternal Mortality Determinants in Nigeria: An Exploratory Study.
scored.why: This exploratory ecological study applied XGBoost and Random Forest machine learning to 64 years of national-level Nigerian data, finding female tertiary education and service-sector employment associated with lower maternal mortality ratios. The ecological, country-level design cannot establish individual-level causation and the analysis is purely associative rather than a clinically actionable predictive tool, limiting its relevance to this reader's clinical AI focus.

scored.title: An integrated deep learning and Bayesian computational method-based quantification of angiogenesis in the chick embryo model.
scored.why: This methods paper developed a combined deep learning and Bayesian hierarchical Gompertz Gaussian process pipeline to quantify angiogenesis in the chick embryo yolk sac membrane (YSM) assay, validated pharmacologically against known pro- and anti-angiogenic agents like vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). It is a preclinical image-analysis tool for a widely used animal-free-ish angiogenesis assay rather than a human clinical or reproductive health study, so its relevance to this reader's beats is limited to methodological interest.

scored.title: Systems-level genomic analyses reveal shared mechanisms underlying endometriosis and sleep disorders.
scored.why: This study combined National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) cross-sectional data, bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR), and expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL)/protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) gene mapping to find a genetic and epidemiologic link between endometriosis and sleep disorders, with machine learning used only briefly for gene prioritization among 37 candidates. The genetic and observational associations (odds ratio 2.64 for sleep disorder prevalence, inverse variance weighted MR odds ratio 1.11) are modest and explicitly framed as hypothesis-generating, with minimal AI methodology central to the findings.

scored.title: [Endometriosis pain research in Germany : ENDO-PAIN and StEPP-UPP-two new research consortia on endometriosis pain].
scored.why: This article describes two new German research consortia, StEPP-UPP and ENDO-PAIN, that plan to use explainable artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning models alongside multi-omics and prospective cohorts to study endometriosis pain mechanisms, but no results, models, or validation data are presented. It is a program announcement rather than an evaluated study, so its value to this reader is mainly as a marker of upcoming infrastructure rather than actionable evidence.

scored.source: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
scored.title: Integrating laboratory tests with FIGO staging using machine learning improves long-term prognostic assessment in endometrial cancer.
scored.why: This single-center retrospective cohort of 760 women with endometrial cancer combined 48 routine laboratory tests with FIGO staging (International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics staging) using ten machine learning models to predict long-term survival, with the best model reaching an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.876 for 10-year overall survival, outperforming stage alone. The small single-center sample, wide confidence intervals, and lack of external validation limit confidence that these gains would replicate elsewhere, and a supplementary Mendelian randomization analysis found no causal link between the biomarkers and cancer risk.

scored.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward artificial intelligence in medicine among Chinese physicians: A cross-sectional study from January to March 2024 with analysis of influencing factors.
scored.why: This nationwide cross-sectional survey of 1,137 Chinese physicians assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward artificial intelligence (AI) in medicine, finding that only 30.4% had good AI knowledge and 28.8% reported good AI practices, with obstetrics/gynecology specialization independently associated with higher odds of good practice (odds ratio 4.95). This is a survey of attitudes and self-reported behavior rather than an evaluation of any actual AI tool or clinical outcome, so its relevance to this reader is limited to context about adoption barriers rather than evidence of clinical utility.

scored.title: A 23-µJ-per-Frame All-on-Chip TinyML U-Net Processor for Real-Time Autonomous Image Segmentation in Miniaturized Ultrasound Devices.
scored.why: This is an engineering paper describing a low-power computer chip that runs a compressed U-Net segmentation model on-device for wearable ultrasound, validated on bladder and fetal head segmentation datasets at 13.4 frames per second (fps) and 23 microjoules per frame. It is a hardware feasibility demonstration, not a clinical evaluation, so its relevance to patient care is speculative though the fetal biometry application is notable.

scored.title: Assessing the Reliability of Large Language Models for Evaluation of Risk of Bias in Randomized Clinical Trials.
scored.why: This retrospective study evaluated large language models (LLMs), including ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet, for automating risk-of-bias (RoB) assessment in 180 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, finding ChatGPT-5 achieved moderate agreement with human reviewers (kappa 0.36-0.40) but all models struggled with selective reporting detection. This is a methods-focused evaluation relevant to evidence synthesis workflows rather than direct patient care, with only moderate concordance limiting its use as a standalone tool.

scored.title: Preoperative prediction of parametrial invasion in early-stage cervical cancer: a radiomics nomogram fusing multi-parametric MRI and clinical biomarkers.
scored.why: This study developed a radiomics nomogram combining multi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features and clinical biomarkers to preoperatively predict parametrial invasion (PMI) in early-stage cervical cancer, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.806-0.827 with external validation in 363 patients. External validation strengthens the finding, but this is an incremental radiomics model with modest external sensitivity (0.583) and no comparison to current clinical staging accuracy.

scored.title: Doctronic Acquires Summer Health to Expand into Pediatric Primary Care
scored.why: Doctronic, an AI-powered primary care platform, acquired Summer Health, a pediatric telehealth service, to expand its offerings into pediatric care. No clinical evidence or AI performance data is presented, only a corporate acquisition announcement.

scored.title: The FDA was all in on AI. Will that change?
scored.why: This piece reports on leadership turnover at the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and its potential to slow the agency's artificial intelligence (AI) strategy, but offers no specifics on policy changes, timelines, or affected clearances. It is a speculative regulatory update rather than a substantive finding.

scored.title: The iPatient Meets the iDoctor.
scored.why: This JAMA piece titled 'The iPatient Meets the iDoctor' has no abstract or text provided, so its content and evidentiary basis cannot be assessed. Given the title, it appears to be a commentary or perspective piece rather than original research, warranting a conservative low score.

scored.title: Explainable machine learning in healthcare: methods, interpretation, and applications for clinical research.
scored.why: This is a methodological primer reviewing explainable machine learning (XML) techniques such as SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME), illustrated on a public heart disease dataset rather than original clinical research. As a tutorial rather than a new evaluation or clinical finding, it offers limited new information for someone already working in clinical AI.

scored.title: Explainability in context: calibrating appropriate trust and reliance in artificial intelligence.
scored.why: This is a conceptual perspective piece proposing a framework of contextual explainability, at the model, setting, subpopulation, and patient level, to help clinicians calibrate trust in artificial intelligence (AI) predictions. It presents no original data or empirical evaluation, so its contribution is a proposed design principle rather than tested evidence.

scored.title: Building safer artificial intelligence mental health chatbots: a framework for transparency, evaluation, and shared accountability.
scored.why: This paper synthesizes existing literature on artificial intelligence (AI) mental health chatbots built on large language models (LLMs) to propose a three-stage governance framework addressing transparency, evaluation, and accountability. It is a policy and governance proposal rather than original clinical or technical evaluation, limiting its direct relevance to this reader's evidence-focused interests.

scored.title: Identification and importance analysis of osteoporosis risk factors in perimenopausal women based on the Transformer-LSTM hybrid model and SMOTE.
scored.why: This retrospective single-center study used a Transformer-long short-term memory (LSTM) hybrid model with synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) to classify osteoporosis risk in perimenopausal women, reporting accuracy of 89.5% and macro area under the curve (AUC) of 0.923, improvements framed relative to weaker single-architecture baselines rather than clinical utility. This is an incremental architecture comparison on one hospital's data without external validation, offering little new clinical insight beyond confirming known risk factors like prior collagen turnover markers.

scored.title: Mechanistic advances in nanomedicine, nucleic acid therapies, and AI-driven research on cervical cancer.
scored.why: This is a narrative review of nanomedicine, nucleic acid therapeutics, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted formulation design for cervical cancer drug delivery, with AI discussed only briefly as one of several emerging tools. It presents no new experimental or clinical evidence and functions as a broad mechanistic overview rather than an evaluable finding.

scored.title: ATF4, ZIK1, and PNMA3 Transcriptomic Signatures Predict Chemoradiotherapy Response in Cervical Cancer.
scored.why: This small retrospective study analyzed RNA sequencing data from 31 cervical cancer patients (21 responders, 10 non-responders) and used machine learning to narrow 2,670 differentially expressed genes down to a three-gene signature (ATF4, PNMA3, ZIK1) associated with chemoradiotherapy response. The sample size is very small for a genomic biomarker discovery study and there is no external validation cohort, so the proposed signature remains a preliminary hypothesis rather than a clinically ready predictor.

scored.source: Zhonghua Fu Chan Ke Za Zhi
scored.title: [Radiomics and deep learning in the prediction of spontaneous preterm birth using cervical ultrasound].
scored.why: This is a title-only record for a study on radiomics and deep learning applied to cervical ultrasound for predicting spontaneous preterm birth, with no abstract or methodological detail provided. Without sample size, validation approach, or performance metrics, it is impossible to assess the strength or novelty of the work.

scored.title: Digital twins in menopause: a roadmap for integrating endocrine dynamics, multisystem physiology, and precision medicine.
scored.why: This is a narrative review proposing that digital twins, computational replicas of individual patients that integrate real-time data with mechanistic and AI-driven modeling, could someday unify endocrine, cardiovascular, skeletal, and neurocognitive changes across the menopausal transition, but it presents no new data, models, or validation. As a conceptual roadmap rather than an evaluated system, it offers limited immediate value to a reader focused on evidence-based clinical AI.

scored.title: Aspartame exposure promotes endometriosis progression through PTGS2-mediated oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction.
scored.why: This bench-based mechanistic study combined toxicity databases, protein-protein interaction network analysis, and machine learning algorithms merely as one step in a broader pipeline to identify PTGS2 as a target gene linking aspartame exposure to endometriosis progression, validated through cell culture and mouse experiments. The machine learning component is incidental to a primarily wet-lab mechanistic investigation, so it offers little direct relevance to clinical AI evaluation despite the biological interest of the aspartame-endometriosis link.

scored.title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Regeneration of Endometrium in Asherman's Syndrome.
scored.why: This is a narrative literature review on treatment strategies for Asherman's syndrome (intrauterine adhesions), with a brief concluding discussion of how artificial intelligence, including machine learning and deep learning, might someday assist in classifying adhesions or improving biomaterials. No original data, models, or validation are presented, making this primarily an educational overview rather than substantive evidence.

scored.title: ASO Special Article: Proceedings of the Inaugural Joint US-India Cancer Dialogue: Accelerating Collaboration to Advance Cancer Prevention, Early Detection, Treatment, and Care.
scored.why: This proceedings article summarizes discussions from the inaugural US-India Cancer Dialogue, a policy and collaboration meeting identifying priority areas including artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled early cancer detection, human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination expansion, and immunotherapy access, but it reports no original research, data, or evaluated AI system. As a summary of a diplomatic and strategic meeting rather than a study, it offers minimal direct evidentiary value to this reader's technical interests.

scored.title: Machine Learning-driven Prediction of Cervical Cancer Cell Viability After Treatment With Thymoquinone, Curcumin, and 5-Fluorouracil.
scored.why: This in vitro study tested cytotoxic and apoptotic effects of thymoquinone, curcumin, and 5-fluorouracil on cervical cancer (HeLa) cells and used several machine learning models, with an artificial neural network performing best, to predict cell viability from dose-response data. The work is purely preclinical laboratory research with machine learning applied as a data-fitting tool rather than a clinically validated diagnostic or predictive system, limiting its relevance to a reader focused on clinical AI evaluation.

scored.title: Prediction of retained placenta in holstein dairy cows based on machine learning approaches: Comparative analysis of risk factors and predictive algorithms.
scored.why: This is a machine learning model predicting retained placenta in Holstein dairy cows using routine farm data, achieving a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.867 via a stacking ensemble; it has no relevance to human reproductive medicine or clinical AI in medicine.

scored.title: Unsupervised clustering analysis unravels the role of systemic inflammatory indices in the prognosis of patients with locally advanced cervical cancer treated with chemoradiation.
scored.why: This retrospective single-center study used unsupervised clustering, an agglomerative hierarchical clustering (AHC) algorithm, on blood inflammatory markers to stratify 152 locally advanced cervical cancer patients into two prognostic groups after chemoradiotherapy. The approach is exploratory, lacks external validation, and the clustering itself is a simple statistical grouping method rather than a predictive clinical tool ready for use.

scored.title: Analysis of fetal MRI data reveals no effect on liver maturation following prenatal alcohol exposure.
scored.why: This retrospective study analyzed fetal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with radiomics-based random forest and logistic regression models to detect effects of prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) on liver development, finding no significant differences and a near-chance area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.40-0.43. The study is a negative finding with small sample sizes (n=21 PAE, n=45 non-PAE) and the AI component performed at chance level, limiting its practical impact.

scored.title: Addressing multiple pregnancies in in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer: Current status, challenges, and solutions.
scored.why: This is a narrative review discussing the challenge of multiple pregnancies from in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer (IVF-ET) and mentions time-lapse imaging with artificial intelligence (AI) as one of two promising directions, alongside molecular biology techniques, but presents no new data or evaluation. It restates known clinical tensions between single embryo transfer (SET) and double embryo transfer (DET) without offering evidence beyond what is already established.

scored.title: Multimodal ultrasound assessment of ovarian reserve.
scored.why: This is a narrative review of multimodal ultrasound techniques, including two-dimensional (2D), three-dimensional (3D), Doppler, shear wave elastography (SWE), contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven imaging, for assessing ovarian reserve, with no new data or evaluation presented. It broadly surveys existing imaging modalities and mentions AI only as one component among several without describing any specific study or result.

scored.title: Startup to Acquisition in 2 Years: Grove AI’s Journey to Transform Clinical Trials
scored.why: This is a brief industry news item about Grove AI, a voice-agent startup for clinical trial patient recruitment, being acquired by Hippocratic AI, with no data on efficacy, trial outcomes, or clinical evidence provided. It is a pure business development story without any evaluation of the technology's real-world performance.

scored.title: The Code Gets You Paid — The Variant Gets You Treated
scored.why: This is an opinion piece arguing that healthcare AI tools optimize for billing codes rather than the specific genetic or clinical detail a physician needs to treat a patient, framed around precision medicine and genomics, with no original data, study, or evaluation presented. It is commentary rather than evidence and falls outside the scope of substantive clinical AI findings this digest prioritizes.

scored.title: Smart Toilet Sensor Startup Is Flush with $10M Funding
scored.why: Throne Science raised a $10 million Series A funding round for an AI-powered toilet camera sensor intended to monitor gut health, hydration, and urinary function as an early warning tool for colorectal cancer. This is a funding announcement with no clinical validation data or evidence of diagnostic accuracy provided.

scored.title: AI, humanity, and the open world of health care: enduring imperatives for the next century.
scored.why: This is a commencement address by Eric Horvitz reflecting broadly on artificial intelligence (AI) and clinician responsibility in healthcare, with no original data, methodology, or evaluation. It is opinion and rhetoric rather than research, so it offers little actionable information for this reader.

scored.title: The Big Mo: staying on the wave in an age of artificial intelligence.
scored.why: This is a commencement address by Kevin B. Johnson using a career-retrospective narrative and a momentum metaphor to discuss AI's impact on biomedical informatics careers, with no original research or data. As pure opinion and career reflection, it holds minimal value for someone tracking clinical AI evidence.

scored.title: Stress Reactions in Bone and Stress Fractures.
scored.why: This is a narrative review of stress-related bone injuries and fracture pathophysiology, with AI mentioned only briefly as a future direction for synthetic computed tomography (CT) generation from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and opportunistic osteoporosis screening. It contains no original AI research, evaluation, or clinical data, and is off-topic for a clinical AI or reproductive health digest apart from a passing mention of pregnancy-related fractures.

scored.title: Use of heart rate variability in prediction of clinical deterioration in critically ill hospitalised adults: a systematic review protocol.
scored.why: This is a systematic review protocol examining heart rate variability (HRV) as a predictor of clinical deterioration in critically ill adults, with no results yet reported and no AI or algorithmic component described. It has no reproductive relevance and no findings to evaluate, so it offers nothing actionable this week.

scored.title: Silkworm synthetic biology: Toolkit development, chassis engineering, and biomanufacturing applications.
scored.why: This is a review of silkworm synthetic biology tools for genetic engineering and biomanufacturing, mentioning artificial intelligence only in passing as a future design aid. It has no clinical, reproductive, or evaluative AI content relevant to this digest.

scored.title: Deep Learning for Automated Classification and Dynamic Risk Prediction of Retained Products of Conception on Postpartum Ultrasound.
scored.why: This item on deep learning classification of retained products of conception on postpartum ultrasound has no available abstract text, so no study design, sample size, or performance metric can be assessed. Given the complete absence of substantive content, it cannot be scored on its merits and defaults to a low score this week.

scored.title: Estradiol surges as dual-purpose mechanisms in evolutionary psychiatry: Neuroendocrine stabilization, stress regulation, and psychosis vulnerability.
scored.why: This is a theoretical review proposing an evolutionary psychiatry framework in which estradiol surges during the reproductive cycle may buffer against psychosis vulnerability, synthesizing existing literature on hormone-neurotransmitter interactions without presenting new data or any artificial intelligence component. It has no relevance to clinical AI evaluation and belongs to basic neuroendocrine theory rather than an evidence-based intervention or diagnostic tool.

scored.title: Microfluidic innovations driving the future of sperm motility and sex sorting techniques.
scored.why: This is a narrative review of microfluidic sperm sorting technologies for assisted reproductive technology (ART), with only a passing mention that future platforms might integrate artificial intelligence (AI); it presents no new data, model, or evaluation of any AI system.

scored.title: Prediction of Spontaneous Preterm Birth in the Second Trimester: Current Models, Limitations, and the Way Forward.
scored.why: No abstract text is available for this review on predicting spontaneous preterm birth in the second trimester, so its content, methods, and findings cannot be assessed. Given the missing information, it cannot be scored on substance and is likely a review rather than new evidence.

scored.title: Establishment of insulin resistance-related ten-gene signature in endometrial cancer and identification of ACTL8 as a prognostic and immunological biomarker.
scored.why: This is a bioinformatics study using public gene expression databases and machine learning feature selection to build a ten-gene prognostic signature linking insulin resistance and endometrial cancer, with no clinical validation or algorithmic evaluation of a deployable tool. It is exploratory molecular biology work with a minor machine learning component used only for gene selection, not a clinical AI application.

scored.title: Daffodil Health Launches No Surprises Act Dispute Management Solution
scored.why: This is a product launch announcement for an AI-powered administrative tool to help payers manage No Surprises Act billing disputes, with no clinical content, patient outcome data, or reproductive health relevance. It is a pure business and workflow automation story unrelated to clinical evidence or reproductive medicine.

scored.title: Spotting Alzheimer’s Years Earlier Through AI and Clinically Meaningful Insights
scored.why: This is a promotional piece describing that tablet-based interaction and speech patterns could theoretically reveal early Alzheimer's signs, but it provides no study design, sample size, or performance metrics. The text reads as marketing copy rather than a reportable finding.

scored.title: How AI Inside Clinical Workflows Is Unlocking Patient Throughput
scored.why: This is an opinion piece about the importance of embedding AI tools within clinical workflows to improve patient throughput, without describing any specific technology, trial, or measured outcome. It offers no data, methodology, or evidence to assess.

scored.title: Temporal Evolution and Projections of Violence Against Women in Brazil: Scenarios from 2013 to 2033.
scored.why: This study uses time-series forecasting, Joinpoint regression, and a Random Forest model to project trends in violence against women in Brazil, with no clinical AI application, reproductive medicine content, or evaluation of a medical tool. It belongs to public health policy analysis, entirely outside the scope of this digest's clinical AI or reproductive health focus.

scored.title: AI Readiness Starts with Solving Healthcare’s Data Fragmentation Problem
scored.why: This is sponsored content summarizing a webinar discussion about healthcare data fragmentation as a barrier to artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, with no original research, product, or evidence presented. It is promotional and off-topic for substantive clinical or reproductive AI news.
